item.title: Neural Surface Reconstruction
item.description:
Neural Surface Reconstruction focuses on turning a sparse set of images into detailed, view-consistent geometry and appearance. It is a good home for mesh snapshots, rendered fly-throughs, depth visualizations, and reconstruction comparisons.

Suggested assets

  • preview.svg or featured.jpg for the homepage showcase
  • qualitative figures comparing inputs, depth, normals, and renderings
  • optional demo video linked via showcase_video or demo_url

View on GitHub

item.title: Generative World Building
item.description:
Generative World Building is the placeholder project space for text-to-3D or text-to-scene research. This page is intended for generated assets, scene compositions, ablation figures, and short teaser videos.

What to put here later

  • prompt and output comparisons
  • multi-view render sheets
  • editing or regeneration workflows

View source repository

item.title: Agentic Scene Reasoning
item.description:
Agentic Scene Reasoning is the home for embodied or multimodal agent projects. Use it for rollout captures, evaluation summaries, and dashboards that explain how the agent perceives, reasons, and acts.

Example assets

  • UI screenshots from agent rollouts
  • benchmark tables and success traces
  • short videos of planning and execution

View source repository

item.title: Controllable Scene Editing
item.description:
Controllable Scene Editing is the place for user-facing systems that modify scenes, assets, and layouts. It is a strong fit for interactive editors, generation-plus-editing pipelines, or design tools with iterative loops.

Example materials

  • before and after image pairs
  • editing timeline or workflow screenshots
  • product-style previews of tools and interfaces

View source repository

item.title: Research Notes on Spatial Agents and Long-Horizon Planning
item.description: These notes outline a working view of spatial agents: models should not only perceive the world but also maintain memory, plan over long horizons, and adapt to structured environments.

item.title: Building a Research Showcase That Feels Like a Product
item.description: When a research lab homepage is treated as a product surface instead of a document dump, visitors understand the work faster. Structure, motion, and preview quality matter as much as text.
